title: Open Quantum Problem 40: the pinching inequality for word averages for all word lengths, and the status of the refined BMV lower bound
description: IQOQI Vienna Open Quantum Problem 40 (Hagele) asks whether tr(A^n B^m) >= p_{n,m}(A,B) >= tr exp(n log A + m log B) for positive matrices A, B, where p_{n,m} is the average trace of all words with n letters A and m letters B. The upper half is false (Cha and Lee, 2026). We prove, for all word lengths, the pinching inequality p_{n,m}(A,B) >= tr(A^n E_A(B)^m) conjectured by T. H. Dinh (2026), who proved the case m = 2. The proof is an exact gap identity, p_{n,m}(A,B) - tr(A^n E_A(B)^m) = m(m-1) int int s^{m-2} tau^n rho(s,tau) ds dtau, with an explicit nonnegative density rho built from the roots of the pencil det(B - s - xi(A - tau)). It yields strictness iff AB != BA, a two-sided corrected bound (exact for m = 2), sign-condition variants, a Jensen form, and a positive moment measure for each fixed m. The identity is a pinched two-variable form of Stahl's theorem (the explicit BMV measure of Heinavaara), proved in full for arbitrary multiplicities. The lower half remains open; we prove it when min(n,m) <= 2, prove a stronger form for rank-one letters, document extensive numerical evidence, and list routes that provably fail. The repository contains the proofs, an independent check with exact arithmetic, code and logs.
